title: Kopia
descript: Kopia is a fast, encrypted, deduplicated backup tool with a web UI: snapshot folders on the NAS into a repository on local disk, S3, Backblaze B2, WebDAV, SFTP, Google Cloud or another Kopia server; schedule snapshots, browse versions, restore files and apply retention policies. Data is encrypted on the NAS before it leaves. The UI is protected by HTTP Basic auth; repository and configuration stay in the application data folder.
important: Requires DockerEngine (installed automatically if missing). Open the app, click 'Open the Kopia web interface' and log in as user `kopia`; the random password is generated on first start and stored in DockerAppData/kopiadocker/config/.server-password (mode 600). Create the repository in the UI - a folder under /data is simplest, S3/B2/WebDAV/SFTP also work - and keep its password: without it snapshots cannot be restored. Plain HTTP; put a TLS reverse proxy in front before exposing it to the internet.
release_note: 2. Rectified per review comments (C2-C8, C10, T1, F5, F10). Public landing page so the App Center can open the app, while the UI itself stays behind HTTP Basic auth; the UI password is no longer printed to the log; PRIVACY.md, NOTICE.md and README.md completed; third-party endpoint table; the repository password is persisted (mode 600) so snapshots survive a restart; update checks and telemetry are off. The pinned image is the newest upstream build.

trial_run.log_tail: the image alone answers 401 Unauthorized (WWW-Authenticate: Basic realm="Kopia", body "Missing credentials.") on every path including /, and refuses to start without an account; as a non-root user it additionally cannot write /app/logs. That is why this package wraps the server (generated password + Caddy landing page on the published port).

wrapper_note: the Kopia server answers 401 on every path (including /) unless an account is supplied, so a random UI password is generated on first start and passed to the server through the environment (never through the log or docker inspect). A second, tiny Caddy container owns the published port: it serves a public 200 landing page on / and proxies everything else to Kopia, which keeps its Basic auth.
wrapper_note_readme:
- **Two containers**: `kopiadocker` runs the Kopia server (uid 1000, no published port) and `kopiadocker-web` runs a Caddy front that serves a public landing page on `/` (HTTP 200) and reverse-proxies the UI, which keeps its HTTP Basic auth.
- **Generated UI password**: created on first start, stored in `config/.server-password` (mode 600) and passed via `KOPIA_SERVER_PASSWORD` - it is never written to the container log.

zh-hk.descript: Kopia 是一款快速、加密、去重的備份工具，自帶網頁介面：把 NAS 上的目錄做成快照，存到本機磁碟、S3、Backblaze B2、WebDAV、SFTP、Google Cloud 或另一台 Kopia 伺服器上的倉庫；支援定時快照、瀏覽歷史版本、還原檔案與保留策略。資料在離開 NAS 之前就已加密。介面受 HTTP Basic 認證保護；倉庫與設定都保存在應用資料目錄。
zh-hk.important: 需要 DockerEngine（缺少時應用中心會自動安裝）。開啟應用後，在引導頁點「Open the Kopia web interface」，用使用者名稱 `kopia` 登入；隨機密碼在首次啟動時產生，保存在 DockerAppData/kopiadocker/config/.server-password（權限 600）。請在介面裡建立倉庫（放在 /data 下最簡單，也可用 S3/B2/WebDAV/SFTP），並記住倉庫密碼——沒有它無法還原快照。介面為純 HTTP，公開到互聯網前請配置帶 TLS 的反向代理。
zh-hk.release_note: 2. 按審核意見整改（C2-C8、C10、T1、F5、F10）。新增公開引導頁，使應用中心能正常開啟，而介面本身仍受 HTTP Basic 認證保護；介面密碼不再列印到日誌；補齊 PRIVACY.md、NOTICE.md 與 README.md；新增第三方端點表；倉庫密碼持久化（權限 600），重啟後快照任務不中斷；關閉更新檢查與遙測。映像仍為上游最新建置。

data_notes: `/config` holds `kopia.config`, `kopia.config.kopia-password` (the repository password, mode 600, written by Kopia when `--persist-credentials` is on), the generated UI password in `.server-password` and the local cache; `/data` (mounted from `.../data`) is the recommended place for a filesystem repository. Nothing else on the NAS is written; the Caddy front keeps its state in the container's /tmp.
design_notes: **Landing page first.** Kopia answers 401 on every path until Basic credentials arrive, so the App Center open check could not even load a login prompt. A Caddy front serves a public, secret-free landing page on `/` (200) and proxies everything else to Kopia; the UI keeps its own auth, and `/snapshots` is where the app entry lands.

**Password generated once, never logged.** No credential is baked into the package: the wrapper creates a random UI password, stores it in the config volume (mode 600) and hands it over in the environment (not in the command line, not in the log).

**Repository created in the UI.** The package does not create a repository; the user picks the storage location and the (separate) repository password. `--persist-credentials` keeps that password in `config/kopia.config.kopia-password` (mode 600) so the server reconnects and scheduled snapshots continue after a restart.

**No telemetry, no update check.** `KOPIA_CHECK_FOR_UPDATES=false` plus `--no-check-for-updates`; Kopia has no analytics. The only outbound traffic is repository traffic to the storage the user configures (plus notification profiles, if the user adds any).
limitations: - The UI is plain HTTP; use a TLS reverse proxy before exposing it to the internet.
- The repository password is persisted locally (mode 600) so restarts keep working; delete `config/kopia.config.kopia-password` if you prefer to re-enter it every time.
- Mounting snapshots as a filesystem is not offered: the container has no FUSE device. Restores are done by downloading the selected files from the UI.
- Snapshot storage grows with the folders you back up; watch free space on the NAS.
